question: Which of the following minerals is responsible for synthesis of thyroxine hormone?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Iodine__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Thyroxin regulates carbohydrate, protein, and fat metabolism in the body to achieve optimal growth balance.
 
• Thyroxine hormone is secreted by the thyroid gland into the bloodstream.
 
• The thyroid gland is the largest endocrine gland.
 
• Thyroxine hormone is an iodinated form of the amino acid (tyrosine).
 
• They are stored in the colloid that fills the follicles and released into the blood when needed.
 
• It then travels to organs such as the liver and kidneys, where it is converted into its active form triiodothyronine.
 
• Iodine (from the diet) is required for the synthesis of thyroxine hormone.
 
• Functions of thyroxine hormone:
 
 
• The thyroid hormone serves several functions in the body, such as
 
• The thyroxine hormone maintains and regulates the Basal Metabolic Rate.
 
• They contribute to the formation of red blood cells.
 
• It also helps in controlling the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.
 
• It has an impact on the maintenance of water and electrolytes in our bodies.
